findings.description: The Lambda function embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key in plain text environment variables. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or console read access can retrieve them, and they are committed to version control, so they must be treated as compromised.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which hold secrets here) are protected only by the default service-owned key rather than a customer-managed KMS key with a controllable key policy and rotation.
The function uses runtime nodejs12.x, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so the deployment package is not signature-verified; tampering with the artefact between build and deployment would not be detected.
